title: Layer-Locked Chiral Topological Superconductivity
abstract: We uncover a universal mechanism for realizing layer-locked topological phases. Guided by it, we investigate the realization of layer-locked chiral topological superconductivity-the superconducting analogue of the quantum anomalous layer Hall effect-in a nonsymmorphic bilayer antiferromagnetic system with s-wave pairing. We identify three distinct gate-tunable topological phases and establish a direct correspondence between the nearly quantized layer-resolved Chern numbers and the layer-locking behavior of chiral Majorana edge states, vortex-core Majorana zero modes, and nearly quantized thermal Hall responses.
summary: The paper proposes a universal mechanism to realize layer-locked chiral topological superconductivity in bilayer antiferromagnets. By tuning an external gate voltage, the system can be driven into three distinct topological phases, each characterized by unique layer-resolved Chern numbers. These theoretical predictions are strongly correlated with observable signatures like confined Majorana edge states and quantized thermal Hall responses.
main_problem: The research aims to uncover a universal mechanism for realizing layer-locked topological phases, specifically focusing on chiral topological superconductivity (CTSC) in bilayer antiferromagnetic systems.
main_result: Three distinct, gate-tunable topological superconducting phases were identified, characterized by unique layer-resolved Chern numbers ($C_t, C_b$) and corresponding physical signatures like edge states and thermal Hall responses.
method: The study uses the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian to model the system and characterizes topology using layer-resolved Chern numbers calculated from the Berry curvature.
model_or_system: A minimal bilayer antiferromagnetic system with s-wave pairing is modeled, featuring nonsymmorphic symmetries that enforce specific hopping vanishing conditions. The Hamiltonian includes terms for hopping, spin-orbit coupling, magnetic fields, and superconducting pairing ($\Delta$).
key_observables: Layer-resolved Chern numbers ($C_t, C_b$), layer-locked chiral Majorana edge states (CMESs), vortex-core Majorana zero modes (MZMs), and the thermal Hall response ($\kappa_{xy}^z$).
important_parameters: Gate voltage tuning of the staggered potential ($V_z$) is crucial for transitioning between the three distinct topological phases.
main_assumptions: The layer-resolved Chern number is noted not to be a genuine topological invariant, and the model relies on specific symmetry constraints (nonsymmorphic symmetries).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of $C, C_t, C_b$ on $V_z$, show layer-resolved probability density profiles for MZMs under vortices in different locking phases, and confirm the quantization of the thermal Hall coefficient ($\kappa_{xy}^z = C\kappa_0$).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using the BdG Hamiltonian, derives the mechanism based on symmetry constraints, identifies three distinct topological superconducting regimes by tuning $V_z$, and validates these findings through multiple measurable physical diagnostics (edge states, vortices, thermal response).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable platform for realizing exotic topological superconductivity using engineered symmetries in layered materials, which is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems.
